name: RigoBlock Drago setMultipleAllowances missing owner check
summary: Drago v2 pools expose setMultipleAllowances(proxy, tokens, amounts) without the onlyOwner and whenApprovedProxy modifiers that guard setAllowance, so anyone can make a pool approve an arbitrary spender for its ERC-20 holdings. The attacker had the Pure Alpha Drago approve its contract for six tokens and then pulled and sold them; a second actor later used the same call on the byte-identical PayRue 1 Drago to take its aDAI.
notes: DragoFactory v2 created the Pure Alpha Drago with the full Drago runtime (no delegation for setMultipleAllowances); the runtime is immutable and owner operations do not affect the missing modifiers. PayRue 1 is a byte-identical sibling exploited later in the same episode.

Exact Drago debits: Pure Alpha 0x682e3e207b18555bc75c072233e7d9fd0c386b9a lost six tokens in source-2 (block 14224068), and PayRue 1 0x98901ce9c337c8663e49a8ba2bc36370990d5e6e lost 78.459636476125759114 aDAI (including interest accrued on transfer) in source-6. Source-2 was sent by generalized front-runner 0x7eb44bf215794d5a44d44b2d8d4a32da2a7a5aea, which replayed the attacker contract's public drain function; the attacker's own copy (0x3ea9d22cda4e34f8fb73b3a79f84be174f2af459d46322e6d5e7903259696bf8) reverted, and the proceeds still went to the attacker contract. Reported whitehat returns and the bounty do not reduce gross loss. Reported totals (SlowMist 160.86 ETH, DefiLlama 464,000 USD) are not reproduced by any Drago debit found; they appear to describe value at risk.
